title.narrative: Somalia - Water for Agro-pastoral Productivity and Resilience

description.narrative: Develop water and agricultural services among agro-pastoralist communities in dryland areas of Somalia.

The development objective of the Water for Agro-Pastoral Productivity and Resilience Project for Somalia is to develop water and agricultural services among agro-pastoralist communities in dryland areas of Somalia. The project comprises of four components. The first component, support the development of multiple use water sources will finance investments in key water management infrastructure for harvesting, storing, and delivering water for people, livestock, and agriculture. It consists of following sub-components: (i) construction of new community water points; and (ii) rehabilitation of community water points. The second component, institutional and capacity development will help build a strong foundation for a gradual transition to more integrated and sustainable agriculture and water development - promoting the farmers adoption of drought-resistant seed varieties and climate-smart technologies - by strengthening local, state, and national institutions and capacities. It consists of following sub-components: (i) national and state institutional capacity building; and (ii) community development and demand mobilization. The third component, supporting sustainable land management and livelihoods development around water points will catalyze priority investments, facilitated by participating Federal Member States (FMS) line ministries, to create and strengthen productive livelihoods among target communities. It consists of following sub-components: (i) integrated landscape management; and (ii) agriculture and livestock support. The fourth component, project management, monitoring and evaluation (M and E), knowledge management, and learning will finance the operational costs of the project management units in participating FMS and Somaliland, as well as project coordination and fiduciary support at the Federal Republic of Somalia (FRS) level. It consists of following sub-components: (i) project management; (ii) M and E, knowledge management, and learning; and (iii) contingent emergency response.

title.narrative: Improved community water points rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative: <p>TARGET PARTIALLY ACHIEVED (68%). The project financed detailed feasibility studies, designs, construction supervision services and procurement of local contractors to undertake the rehabilitation of one <em>haffir</em> dam in South west FMS and boreholes in Galmudug and Puntland FMS. The specific locations where the infrastructures were constructed are described under the Key Outputs section of Annex 1 of the ICR. The rehabilitation included repair of non-functioning components of existing boreholes and expansion of infrastructure by increasing their water storage capacity, constructing more water kiosks and livestock troughs, and in some cases retrofitting existing diesel-powered generator sets with solar pumping systems. Data source: review of construction completion reports provided by the FMS PIUs, the project’s third-party M&E agency – CARE International through the MIS and endline survey report prepared by the FGS PIU. </p>

title.narrative: Improved community water points constructed under the project

comment.narrative: <p>TARGET PARTIALLY ACHIEVED (76%). The project financed detailed feasibility studies, designs, construction supervision services and procurement of local contractors to undertake the construction of 34 various technologies for surface run-off water harvesting and storage infrastructures including haffir dams, sand dams and sub-surface dams in various locations across the three FMS of Galmudug, Puntland and South West. The specific locations where the infrastructures were constructed are described under the Key Outputs section of Annex 1 of the ICR. 11 of the earlier planned water sources in Puntland were not complete due to cost escalations resulting from exogenous factors to the project. Data source: review of construction completion reports provided by the FMS PIUs, the projectrsquo;s third-party M&E agency – CARE International through the MIS, and end-line survey report prepared by the FGS PIU</p>

title.narrative: People provided with access to improved water sources under the project

comment.narrative: <p>TARGET ACHIEVED (145%) AND FEMALE TARGET SUBSTANTIALLY ACHIEVED (98%). To achieve this result, the project financed the construction of 34 new water sources and rehabilitated 15 existing water sources in the three FMS of Galmudug, Puntland and South West at various sites as indicated in the key outputs section of Annex 1. The project financed relevant surveys, feasibility studies, and designs; Cost for the construction of the 49 completed water sources including the construction of all appurtenant structures (animal troughs, water tanks, storage tanks, and distribution pipelines; purchase and installation of water pumps, and solar pumping systems. Data source: review of construction completion reports provided by the FMS PIUs, the project’s third-party M&E agency – CARE International through the MIS, and the endline survey report prepared by the FGS PIU.</p>

title.narrative: Number of PIUs established under the project and functioning

comment.narrative: <p>TARGET ACHIEVED (100%) AND FEMALE TARGET PARTIALLY ACHIEVED (44%). The result reflects one PIU formed at the FGS within the MoPIED (five female and 13 male members), and one PIU each in the three participating FMS of Galmudug (four female and 13 male members), Puntland (three female and 12 male members), and South West (three female and 16 male members), housed within the FMS Ministry of Panning and drawing membership from relevant participating line ministries. In addition to these 69 core PIU members, 62 government staff (17 female and 45 males) who are experts in various fields related to water and agricultural services were periodically seconded to support the PIU members in undertaking various project activities. The project financed the cost of hiring external experts into the PIUs to complement capacity gaps among government staff members of the PIUs and also provided the cost of logistics for the PIU members to undertake their responsibilities including purchase of vehicles, construction of new and rehabilitation of existing offices including the purchase of ICT equipment in addition to the provision of field allowances for PIU staff while undertaking their project related duties. Data source: Annual project progress reports and the Endline survey report prepared by the FGS PIU.</p>

title.narrative: Number of Community Management Systems Established

comment.narrative: <p>TARGET ACHIEVED (120%). The result reflects 54 community management systems, namely community committees, including village, farmer, women, youth, water management, social, and pastoralist development committees across the three FMS. The selection of the committee members was guided by standard criteria that were applied across the FMS. The criteria included the inclusion of at least one female member per committee, each committee had to have a chairman, secretary, treasurer, and a GBV and GRM focal point. The committees formed had a total membership of 1,947 (1,178 males and 769 females) with Galmudug, Puntland, and South West FMS having 530, 992, and 425 members of different committees respectively. The project funds were used to provide different training types to equip theommittees with the necessary skills to participate in project planning and implementation monitoring during implementation and skills to oversee management and maintenance of project outputs beyond the project period. Data source: Community Engagement Reports prepared by each FMS PIU, quarterly and annual project progress reports and the Endline survey report prepared by the FGS PIU.</p>

title.narrative: Target beneficiaries satisfied with project investments.

comment.narrative: <p>TARGET ACHIEVED (114%). This indicator measured the satisfaction level of the beneficiaries with the different activities financed under the project. Different satisfaction dimensions were assessed including increased water quantity during the dry season compared to the pre-intervention period, increased water quality during the wet season compared to the pre-intervention period, reduced time spent to fetch water, the ability of the government to provide water for humans consumption/domestic uses, and the ability of the government to support the provision of water for livestock and for agriculture purposes. Other dimensions include the agricultural inputs distributed (seeds and tools), livestock treatment services provided by the mobile VET clinics, and rangeland rehabilitation The respondents who were household members sampled from different project sites across all three FMS were asked how satisfied he/she is with the investments on a four-point Likert scale as follows: On a scale of 1-5, how can you rate your satisfaction with the Biyoole project investment? (1=Least satisfied, 5= Very Satisfied). For each response, an average was computed, and the weighted averages of all responses were converted to a percentage. Data source: the project’s third-party M&E agency – CARE International through the MIS and end-line survey report prepared by the FGS PIU in 2023.</p>

title.narrative: Number of PIU members trained disaggregated by (male/female)

comment.narrative: <p>TARGET ACHIEVED (173%) AND FEMALE TARGET SUBSTANTIALY ACHIEVED (73%). Project funds were sued to facilitate training workshops for the PIU members on various areas including project management sing different world bank safeguards, procurement, and financial management instruments. Annex 7 of this ICR details the specific training areas completed. Data source: PIU training reports prepared by the FGS PIU, Quarterly project progress reports provided by the FMS PIUs, the project’s third-party M&E agency – CARE International through the MIS and end-line survey report prepared by the FGS PIU.</p>

<p>TARGET WAS SUBSTANTIALLY ACHIEVED (98%) AND THE FEMALE TARGET WAS PARTIALLY ACHIEVED (84%). The project aimed to reach 80% of 150,000 beneficiaries with agricultural services. At closing, the project reached 117,575 farmers (17,664 in Galmudug, 63,491 in Puntland and 36,420 in South west FMS) with agricultural services so that they can be equipped with the necessary skills, knowledge, and support services to leverage the opportunity of more available water to engage in crop and livestock production. Data source: Quarterly project progress reports provided by the FMS PIUs, the project’s third-party M&E agency – CARE International through the MIS and end-line survey report prepared by the FGS PIU.</p>

<p>TARGET PARTIALLY ACHIEVED (77% overall, 82% of female target). The result reflects the number of targeted beneficiaries who leveraged the availability of water to engage in more crop farming and livestock production activities. Adoption was defined as a farmer practising at his/her own farms the different improved technology introduced to him/her by the project. The project funded the traiing of agro-pastoralists in the three FMS of Galmudug, Puntland, and South West in animal health management, proper grazing techniques, innovative techniques for fodder production, improved dryland farming techniques including techniques for land preparation using a conservation agriculture approach and planting a dryland variety of crops, how to select drought-tolerant crop and seed varieties, and various soil and water conservation measures at on-farm demonstration sites. In addition, project funds were used to purchase and distribute farm tools and equipment, seeds, to enhance veterinary laboratories and provide mobile veterinary clinics to treat a variety of animal diseases. Data source: the project’s third-party M&E agency – CARE International through the MISnd end-line survey report prepared by the FGS PIU. </p>
